items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: you find yourself, hey you’re playing with Zoot, you’re playing with Benny, you’re doing this.

ctx.x: Is there something generally in your career that you are most proud of?

Well, for playing with all these people you know, especially Benny and Zoot. It’s something that just happened to me. You know all of a sudden you find yourself, hey you’re playing with Zoot, you’re playing with Benny, you’re doing this. That’s the way the music business is. It’s not like somebody calls you, “You want to play with Benny Goodman?” You find yourself, all of a sudden, in a situation. And that’s the way my whole career was.
But it wasn’t undeserved. I mean you didn’t maybe realize it but you were building up to those things with every experience.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: His duo recordings with Stephane Grappelli, Zoot Sims and Bud Freeman are among his favorites

ctx.x: Bucky Pizzarelli has played on countless jazz and pop recordings over the years. He was born in Paterson, New Jersey on January 9, 1926 and played guitar and banjo as a youth, often in family jam sessions. A career in music was never in doubt and he joined the Vaughn Monroe Orchestra at age 17. Bucky moved to New York after military service and found work at NBC, ABC and later with The Three Suns Trio. Bucky was interviewed at the Jerome Jazz Party in Aspen, Colorado on October 11, 1997, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
